request.system:
You are an extraction engine for transcripts of the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central launch event videos.
You read machine-generated captions that carry a timestamp (seconds) per segment and you return structured JSON.

Hard rules:
- Use only what the transcript says. Do not add product knowledge, context or guesses from outside the transcript.
- Every timestamp you return must be a segment start time "t" that exists in the input, or lie inside a segment's range. Never invent timestamps.
- Quotes must be verbatim substrings of a segment text (same words, same order; you may trim the start and end). 8 to 25 words each. No paraphrasing, no fixing grammar, no stitching segments.
- Status is only what is said or shown in this video: "preview" if they say preview, public preview, beta or similar; "ga" if they say generally available, GA, out of preview, released; "announced" if it is mentioned as coming later, not in this release, roadmap; "unclear" if nothing is said. Always give the quote that proves the status, or null.
- Names of presenters are "as heard"; mark confidence low when the captions could have mangled them.
- No em-dashes anywhere in your text. Use a plain hyphen.
- Write summaries in plain language, no hype words copied from the video (no "exciting", "powerful", "seamless").

output.summary: This window covers the second half of the AL and tools session, built around a sample late fee app. It starts with limits on reading public resources by app ID, then shows how to change a sequence field to big integer and what the compiler and AppSourceCop warn about. It then covers translations with namespaces and several small clarity changes: action tooltip inheritance, audit name system fields, IsDirty and read isolation. The last part shows data-driven tests, test handlers and a static call graph analysis in the AL .NET tool. Two of these topics point to separate sessions with links in the description.

chapters.title: Big integer sequences and extension indexes
Small clarity changes: tooltips, audit names, IsDirty
Test handlers and default test handlers

features.name: Public resource access by app ID
features.description: Getting a resource from another app by app ID only works for public resources. Asking for a private resource or one that does not exist gives an error, so a dependency breaks if the other app stops shipping the resource. Your own private resources still work with the normal functions without an app ID.
caveats: Taking hard dependencies on specific apps' public resources is risky because removing the resource causes an error
Requesting a non-existing resource raises an error

features.name: Change field type from integer to big integer
features.description: A field such as a ledger or sequence entry number can be switched from integer to big integer in an extension when numbers run out. AppSourceCop and the version comparison warn about implicit conversions and possible runtime overflow, but the change is allowed without copying data or keeping a parallel implementation.
caveats: Changing the type does not change the other places where the value is used, for example assigning it to an integer field
Dependent apps that have not changed to big integer can overflow at runtime
prerequisites: AppSourceCop and comparison against the previous app version to see the warnings

features.name: Extension fields mixed with base fields in an index
features.description: With the changes in how the SQL side of extensions is managed, an extension field can now be combined with a base field in one key. This gives an index that is useful for reading data by the new policy group field.

features.name: Namespaces in translations
features.description: Translation XLIFF files can now be generated with fully qualified names (including the namespace) as the ids instead of hash keys built from the name. This avoids collisions between objects with the same name in different namespaces and makes the ids readable.
caveats: Old hash-key ids could collide when names exist more than once in the global space
prerequisites: Translation file setting in app.json for translations with namespaces

features.name: Action inherits page tooltip
features.description: An action that uses RunObject no longer needs its own tooltip, because the tooltip comes from the target page. The description is kept in one place and reused across many pages.

features.name: Audit name system fields (created by / modified by full name)
features.description: New system fields on the record hold the created by and modified by full names next to the user ids. They can be placed on pages in code and are now customizable through personalization or customization, which was hard before because they were only rendered in the client.

features.name: IsDirty on Record and RecordRef
features.description: A new IsDirty method on Record and RecordRef tests whether a record has changed. It lets you ask the user whether to save, instead of comparing fields by hand.

features.name: Explicit read isolation for isolated storage
features.description: Read isolation is now an explicit option when reading from isolated storage. You can state read committed with an update lock instead of leaving it implied. It is only mentioned briefly in the summary.

features.name: Data-driven tests (test data source)
features.description: One test method can run many scenarios taken from a data test source that lists test cases, such as overdue, not overdue and rounding. The data for each case is built on demand, and the platform runs the test once for every entry in the data set.
caveats: Only the new syntax is shown here; a dedicated session in the launch event covers data-driven testing in depth
prerequisites: A data test source implementing the list of test cases

features.name: Test run from command line with structured JSON output
features.description: The whole test suite can be run from the command line. It returns structured JSON with pass, fail and skip counts and a real exit code, so a failed assertion fails the build.

features.name: Test handlers (test lifecycle hooks)
features.description: Test handlers keep setup and reporting out of the test logic. A handler is specified on the test codeunit and offers hooks before and after the test codeunit run, the test procedure run and each test case run. The demo uses a logger handler that traces while tests run.
prerequisites: Handler implementing the test handler interface/enum implementation

features.name: Default test handlers
features.description: A default test handler can be added by extending the default test handlers enum with an implementation, so it covers all test cases that run. It can implement just one hook, such as before test codeunit run, and be used next to handlers on a specific test codeunit.
caveats: A warning appears when only some methods are implemented because there is a default implementation that must be overridden for custom behavior
prerequisites: Enum extension of the default test handlers enum with an implementation of the test handler

features.name: Static call graph analysis (AL .NET tool graph command)
features.description: The AL .NET tool gets a graph command that builds a call graph across an extension and its dependencies. You or a coding agent can query it to see who can call an internal procedure and which public entry points to review. It is a static offline analysis, so outputs can be compared between versions.
caveats: Extraction compiles all specified apps and takes time, so it was done in advance for the demo
Static data differs from the LSP, which looks at the project as it is now
A full session on this is planned, with a link in the description
prerequisites: Extraction of the apps to be queried beforehand

quotes.text: So we made it possible for you to switch to big integer by changing the type.
quotes.why_it_matters: States the design decision to allow changing a field to big integer for large customers whose entries run out of numbers.

quotes.text: but it's still allowed and it will still pass through and you can actually do this change without having to copy data
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows the type change passes the breaking-change check and needs no data copy or parallel implementation.

quotes.text: This will now generate XL files with a fully qualified name as the ids.
quotes.why_it_matters: Describes the namespace-aware translation ids that avoid collisions between same-named objects.

quotes.text: These are not fields that I have created. They're part of the system fields on the record now.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains that created by and modified by full names are new built-in system fields, not custom ones.

quotes.text: run the whole suite from the command line and get structured JSON with pass fail and skip counts plus a real exit code
quotes.why_it_matters: Gives the concrete CI outcome: structured results and an exit code that fails the build.

quotes.text: So for every single entry that exists in this data set, this platform will execute this test and provide the result for it.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains how data-driven tests run: one test method executes once per data set entry.

quotes.text: So I have the flexibility of handling things outside the test case in a common way both globally but also specifically for a specific test code unit.
quotes.why_it_matters: Summarizes that test handlers work at both global and per-codeunit level.

quotes.text: This is a static thing that we can do offline as long as we extract uh the information that we need to query on beforehand.
quotes.why_it_matters: States the call graph is an offline static analysis that needs an up-front extraction step.
